messages:
Ava M.: quick sync — we need a 3-slide microbench pack (social + blog excerpt + webinar hero) that tells the latency->cost story in <30s. goal: clear CTA to demo signup and a short opt-in for the webinar.
Jon R.: can you remind me which model/seq we benchmarked for the headline? 8k seq on rdx-8x?
Ava M.: jon — yes, rdx-v2-8k @ p95 180ms on hosted for the short prompt slice. cost delta vs baseline (open-llm) is ~0.23 tokens->$ conversion for typical prompt. need a simple line: “>2x throughput at comparable cost” or maybe avoid > phrasing.
Maya (Design): want to mock 3 visual hooks: 1) latency tile (p95 + sparkline) 2) token-cost waterfall 3) fallback routing diagram. low-fi OK. Sam G.: for inbound, route demo clicks from bench blog to funnel: demo form -> product-qualify -> schedule. webinar regs to nurture sequence with case study.
Ellie (Growth): suggested messaging A/B: A) “Faster responses, lower unit cost” B) “Same accuracy, less spend” — which one is closer to truth?
Jon R.: accuracy/quality parity is tricky to claim. Better: “High-throughput serving with predictable unit economics.” keeps it true.
Maya (Design): sample copy for the first slide?
Jon R.: how about two options:
- short: “Latency-first serving, predictable token economics.”
- social: “Ship faster LLM features — half the latency, better unit economics.”
Ava M.: Jon’s short headline + a subline with concrete numbers: p95 180ms, typical prompt cost $0.007, ~1.9x throughput vs baseline. Include a tiny footnote: ‘baseline = open-llm standard runtime, 8k seq.’
benchbot: benchmark-run-176800: artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/176800/run-1.
Sam G.: benchbot — awesome. @eng-prod can we get the chart exports as SVG + PNG? need crisp axes for blog and social.
Ava M.: @Maya — pls use muted palette, highlight latency in primary brand color, cost waterfall in accent. keep annotations minimal.
Maya (Design): will do. ETA: EOD tomorrow for low-fi, EOD Fri for final.
Ellie (Growth): landing flow: blog CTA -> /bench-demo?src=blog -> capture company size + use-case -> qualify for sales outreach if ARR > $500k. small companies get automated onboarding. Sam, can you own routing rules?
Sam G.: yes. will add rules and QA by Thu.
Jon R.: for the blog excerpt, add a two-paragraph narrative: 1) problem (latency/cost tradeoffs) 2) what we measured + outcome + next steps (demo/webinar). keep it <250 words.
Ava M.: also want a 30–45s tweet thread + 60s LinkedIn short. Jon, Ellie — can you draft the socials?
Ellie (Growth): drafting now. quick draft for tweet: “Bench highlights: p95 180ms on rdx-v2-8k, ~1.9x throughput vs baseline, predictable token costs. Demo/signup -> link. #inference #LLMops”
Jon R.: tweak: remove model name from tweet, keep numbers + CTA. longform blog will include model and methodology.
Maya (Design): re: charts — small code block for chart settings I used for exports: 
```
chartConfig = { width: 800, height: 320, dpi: 2, x: 'sequence_length', y: 'p95_latency_ms', series: ['redwood', 'baseline'] }
```
can export with --format svg/png.
Ava M.: perfect. final asks: 1) Jon — blog draft by tomorrow noon, 2) Maya — low-fi by EOD, final by Fri, 3) Sam — routing QA by Thu, 4) Ellie — socials + email copy by EOD tomorrow.
Sam G.: noted.
Jon R.: I'll add an optional CTA variant for enterprise: “Request dedicated capacity and SLA-backed latency.”
Ellie (Growth): for webinar signup, add a question: "Are you evaluating inference for product features or cost optimization?" to route to appropriate nurture.
Ava M.: thanks all — sync in #marketing tomorrow 9:30 if needed. react here once you’ve completed your item :thumbsup:.
